types.label: Unknown device
types.head: A device nothing matched.
types.tip: Seeing it everywhere you go? WATCH it.

types.label: Flock (plate cameras)
types.head: License-plate camera.
types.tip: Sold for plates; police use it to track people too.

types.label: Police body cams
types.head: Police body-cam gear nearby.
types.tip: Means police gear is near, not who is filming you.

types.label: Camera glasses
types.head: Camera glasses, maybe.
types.tip: Look for glasses with a small LED on the frame.

types.label: Card skimmers
types.head: The chip inside card skimmers.
types.tip: At a pump or ATM? Don't use it. Tell the clerk.

types.label: Gunshot sensors
types.head: Gunshot-detection sensor.
types.tip: It listens all the time, usually from a pole or roof.

types.label: AirTag
types.head: Someone's Find My tracker.
types.tip: Not yours and been with you a while? Check bags and the car.

types.label: Drones
types.head: A drone, with its ID.
types.tip: When it sends one, INFO shows where the pilot is standing.

types.label: Other plate readers
types.head: License-plate reader.
types.tip: Logs every passing plate into a shared database.

types.label: Cameras
types.head: A camera's radio.
types.tip: In a rental? Look around the room for a lens.

types.label: Samsung SmartTag
types.head: Someone's Samsung SmartTag.
types.tip: Not yours and been with you a while? Check bags and the car.

types.label: Google Find Hub tags
types.head: A Find My Device tracker.
types.tip: Not yours and been with you a while? Check bags and the car.

types.label: Tile
types.head: Someone's Tile tracker.
types.tip: Not yours and been with you a while? Check bags and the car.

types.label: Ring
types.head: A Ring doorbell or camera.
types.tip: Police can ask its owner for footage via Neighbors.

types.label: Deauth flood
types.head: Someone kicking WiFi users off.
types.tip: WiFi may drop. Don't rejoin networks you don't know.

types.label: Evil twin
types.head: A fake copy of a WiFi network.
types.tip: Don't join the open one. Use your phone's data instead.

types.label: Proximity beacons
types.head: A store or venue beacon.
types.tip: Only apps you installed can use it. Check app permissions.

types.label: Hacking tools
types.head: A wireless hacking tool.
types.why: A KNOWN TOOL NAME OR ADDRESS
types.tip: Usually a hobbyist. Watch for odd popups or WiFi drops.

types.label: LoRaWAN
types.head: A long-range sensor network.
types.tip: Meters and sensors report over it. Nothing to do.

types.label: My alerts
types.head: A WiFi name you watch for.
types.tip: Anyone can name a network this. Check where it is.

types.label: Smart speakers
types.head: A smart speaker with mics.
types.tip: In a rental? Ask the host about it, or unplug it.

devices.title: FLIPPER ZERO
devices.head: A Flipper Zero.
devices.tip: Phone popping up fake pairing alerts? This may be why.

devices.title: PWNAGOTCHI
devices.head: A Pwnagotchi WiFi catcher.
devices.tip: A strong WiFi password is what beats it.

devices.title: PINEAPPLE
devices.head: A WiFi Pineapple.
devices.tip: Don't join open networks you don't recognize.

devices.title: DEAUTHER
devices.head: A WiFi deauther.
devices.tip: WiFi keeps dropping? This may be the cause.

devices.title: HAK5 ADDRESS
devices.head: Maybe Hak5 gear.
devices.tip: A hint only. Anyone can set this address.

devices.title: FLOCK POWER
devices.head: A Flock camera's battery.
devices.tip: A Flock camera is on a pole nearby.

devices.title: FLOCK SETUP
devices.head: A Flock camera being set up.
devices.tip: A new camera may be going in here.

devices.title: FLOCK CAMERA
devices.head: Plate-reader camera on a pole.
devices.tip: Police use it to find and follow people, not just cars.

devices.title: FLOCK BLE
devices.head: Bluetooth from Flock gear.
devices.tip: A lead, not proof. Look for a pole camera.

devices.title: FLOCK HOTSPOT
devices.head: A Flock camera's own WiFi.
devices.why: A NETWORK FLOCK CAMS PUT UP
devices.tip: Near a pole camera, it is almost surely that one.

devices.title: LITEON CHIP
devices.head: A chip Flock sometimes uses.
devices.tip: Millions of laptops use it too. A maybe.

devices.title: WIFI MODULE
devices.head: A chip Flock sometimes uses.
devices.tip: Plenty of gadgets use it. A maybe.

devices.title: FACTORY MAC
devices.head: A chip on its factory settings.
devices.tip: Flock cameras ship like this; so do some others.

devices.title: FLOCK MAYBE
devices.head: Possibly Flock gear.
devices.tip: Not proven. Look for a pole camera.

devices.title: AXON BODY 2 / 3 / 4
devices.head: An Axon body camera.
devices.tip: A camera is near, not necessarily pointed at you.

devices.title: AXON NETWORK
devices.head: Police field equipment.
devices.tip: A camera, a charging dock or a car system is nearby.

devices.title: AXON TASER
devices.head: An Axon body cam or TASER.
devices.tip: Police gear is nearby.

devices.title: AXON BODYCAM
devices.head: Maybe an Axon body camera.
devices.tip: A lead, not proof.

devices.title: FLEET ROUTER
devices.head: A vehicle's WiFi router.
devices.tip: Patrol cars use them, and so do buses and trucks.

devices.title: AXON SIGNAL
devices.head: A body-cam trigger sensor.
devices.tip: It tells nearby body cams to start recording.

devices.title: AXON BODY CAM
devices.head: An Axon body camera.
devices.tip: If a camera is recording here, it is this.

devices.title: BODYWORN
devices.head: A body-cam start button.
devices.tip: An officer's camera is nearby.

devices.title: WATCHGUARD
devices.head: A Motorola police camera.
devices.tip: A body cam or in-car video is nearby.

devices.title: DIGITAL ALLY
devices.head: A police or fleet camera.
devices.tip: A body cam or in-car video is nearby.

devices.title: MOTOROLA
devices.head: Maybe a plate reader.
devices.tip: Could also be a police radio.

devices.title: GENETEC
devices.head: A plate reader, often on a car.
devices.tip: Parking and patrol cars carry them.

devices.title: HC-05 MODULE
devices.head: The chip inside card skimmers.
devices.tip: At a pump or ATM? Don't use it. Tell the clerk.

devices.title: RN42 MODULE
devices.head: A Bluetooth serial chip.
devices.tip: Near a card reader? Take a second look.

devices.title: BT04-A
devices.head: A Bluetooth serial chip.
devices.tip: Near a card reader? Take a second look.

devices.title: LINVOR
devices.head: A skimmer-style chip.
devices.tip: Near a card reader? Don't use it.

devices.title: BT SERIAL
devices.head: A Bluetooth serial link.
devices.tip: Printers do this too. Where you are is the tell.

devices.title: WYZE
devices.head: A Wyze camera.
devices.tip: Often aimed at doors and driveways.

devices.title: SIMPLISAFE
devices.head: SimpliSafe security gear.
devices.tip: A camera, a doorbell or the alarm itself.

devices.title: WYZE MODULE
devices.head: Maybe a Wyze camera.
devices.tip: Other gadgets use it too.

devices.title: AMAZON
devices.head: An Amazon device.
devices.tip: A Blink or Ring camera, or just an Echo.

devices.title: HIKVISION
devices.head: A Hikvision camera.
devices.tip: Common CCTV in shops and apartments.

devices.title: REALTEK
devices.head: Maybe a cheap camera.
devices.tip: Routers and TVs use it too. A weak guess.

devices.title: ARLO
devices.head: An Arlo security camera.
devices.tip: Usually outside, on a house.

devices.title: BLINK
devices.head: A Blink camera.
devices.tip: A porch, a window or a doorbell.

devices.title: TUYA
devices.head: A Tuya smart device.
devices.tip: Could be a camera, a plug or a bulb.

devices.title: VERKADA
devices.head: A Verkada camera.
devices.tip: Cloud cameras in schools, offices and shops.

devices.title: AVIGILON
devices.head: An Avigilon camera.
devices.tip: Business and city video.

devices.title: AXIS
devices.head: An Axis network camera.
devices.tip: Shops, transit and city CCTV.

devices.title: I-PRO
devices.head: An i-PRO camera.
devices.tip: CCTV, and some police body cams.

devices.title: DASHCAM
devices.head: A dashcam's own WiFi.
devices.tip: A car nearby is filming the road ahead.

devices.title: FLEET CAMERA
devices.head: A delivery-fleet camera.
devices.tip: Vans and trucks: road and driver cameras.

devices.title: HIDDEN CAMERA
devices.head: A cheap camera in setup mode.
devices.tip: In a rental? Look around the room for a tiny lens.

devices.title: RAY-BAN META
devices.head: Ray-Ban Meta camera glasses.
devices.tip: A small white LED on the frame means it's recording.

devices.title: META DEVICE
devices.head: Camera glasses, or a VR headset.
devices.tip: Look for glasses before worrying.

devices.title: LUXOTTICA
devices.head: Maybe camera glasses.
devices.tip: Ray-Ban and Oakley's maker builds Meta's glasses.

devices.title: SPECTACLES
devices.head: Snap Spectacles.
devices.tip: Camera glasses that record short clips.

devices.title: ROKID
devices.head: Maybe Rokid glasses.
devices.tip: Some models have cameras; some don't.

devices.title: VUZIX
devices.head: Vuzix smart glasses.
devices.tip: Many models have a camera.
